note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: See true rough-dropseed habitat and tuft in gallery panels 3 and 15 (indices 2,14), the original sourced upper flowering sheath in panel 5 (index 4), and developing/mature tightly CONTRACTED but BRANCHED PANICLES in panels 6–7 (indices 5–6). Panel 4 (index 3) is a separate source-determined narrow-panicle close-up. A narrow spike-like head alone does NOT distinguish S. clandestinus from S. compositus, and none of these pictures proves attached perennial roots.
tiles.short: A tight spike-like PANICLE, not a true spike
tiles.status: ACTUAL HABIT AND TIGHT BRANCHED HEAD COVERED — ROOTED VOUCHER MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · ROOT AND TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: The first CC0 image panel 1 (index 0) shows a REAL outside blade/sheath junction and several fine hairs, but not a true inner 0.2–0.3 mm fringe with a 1-mm bar. Bob Harms' two-view collar photo is panel 14 (index 13), with source scale at right; individual hair tips cannot safely be measured from those pixels. Panel 3 (index 2) shows aboveground tuft foliage only. Require an exposed basal fibrous root/crown connected to a flowering culm, plus a sharply focused, opened INNER fringe ligule next to calibrated 0.5–1 mm graduations.
tiles.short: Perennial crown; a 0.2–0.3 mm hair fringe
tiles.status: TWO REAL COLLAR VIEWS — TRUE MEASURED INNER HAIR FRINGE AND ROOT CROWN STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE ONE SPIKELET
tiles.details: Panels 8 and 10–11 (indices 7,9,10) show PURPLE ANTHERS exerted beyond actual green/lilac flowering units; they are pollen organs, NOT awns. Bob Harms' panel 13 (index 12) shows genuine intact/opened one-floret spikelet and separately isolated pale grains and floral bracts. Approx. 5–7 mm spikelet size and one fertile floret are PUBLISHED botanical measurements; the photographed parts have not been jointly measured and assigned to one authenticated collected individual.
tiles.short: 5–7 mm, one fertile floret, no awn
tiles.status: TRUE FLOWERING ORGANS AND SPIKELET PHOTOGRAPHED — SAME-VOUCHER 1-MM MEASUREMENT MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES AND FERTILE LEMMA
tiles.details: A real author-identified dissected material photograph appears at panel 13 (index 12) and Cleveland Powell's separately sourced spikelet image at panel 12 (index 11). The source shows multiple detached floral pieces and pale grains, but pixel resolution and continuity do not justify assigning lower/upper glume or fertile lemma/palea to arbitrary fragments. Kew descriptions give shorter stiff one-veined outer glumes and an awnless, pubescent lemma; isolate a measured intact spikelet and annotate each physically exposed part only after expert cross-check.
tiles.short: Rough outer glumes, pubescent inner lemma
tiles.status: ACTUAL DISSECTION PRESENT — IDENTIFIED SEPARATED GLUMES/LEMMA/PALEA UNCONFIRMED

tiles.heading: 05 · GRAIN AND MICROSCOPIC PROOF
tiles.details: Harms' source photograph in panel 13 (index 12) shows dry grains, NOT a demonstrated wet-test response. Separately published SPORO research finds that fresh mature *S. clandestinus* pericarps may loosen when wet without the marked gelatinous slipping often seen in *S. compositus*, and its lemma bears characteristic intercostal prickles at microscopy scale. These observations are species-study links only; the Monocots collection's credited educational permission is NOT blanket republication of SPORO research images. Older grains may test differently, and the character is never certified from ordinary dry-panicle photographs.
tiles.short: Fresh wet pericarp and 400× lemma prickles
tiles.status: DRY GRAIN PHOTOGRAPHED — MATCHED WET TEST AND 400× LEMMA MICROSCOPE PENDING

tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Gallery panel 16 (index 15) is explicitly *S. compositus*; panel 17 (index 16) explicitly *S. vaginiflorus*. They are different-taxon comparisons, NOT *S. clandestinus* anatomy. Rough and composite dropseed can both be perennial with similar contracted panicles (see panel 7, index 6). Poverty dropseed is generally a smaller annual; root system and sheltered spikelets help but are not decisive alone. Mature glumes/lemma, timed fresh-grain wet behavior, and microscopy may be required for rough-versus-composite; avoid species certification from a short tight head or local name.
tiles.short: Do not remove a dropseed from panicle silhouette
tiles.status: ACTUAL TWO LOOK-ALIKE PHOTOS IN GALLERY — DIAGNOSTIC MATCHED GRAIN/LIGULE SERIES PENDING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: ROUGH DROPSEED (*Sporobolus clandestinus*): find a perennial fine-leaved tuft, then the long narrow tightly CONTRACTED but BRANCHED PANICLE; Bob Harms SPCL-a1 (field tufts), SPCL-I/i1 (green to mature narrow panicle) and SPCL-b (same above-ground upper culm with partly sheathed blooming head) show real source species, not Hays specimen proof. Learn genuinely EXSERTED PURPLE ANTHERS in J/J1/J2, then isolate ONE single-FLORETED AWNLESS spikelet in source SPCL-S, showing small outer glumes, inner lemma/palea and detached pale actual grains; treat tiny subparts cautiously until precise arrow QA. The real blade/sheath junction SPCL-L is a source-scale reference to ~0.2–0.3mm ligule HAIR FRINGE (NOT large membrane). Most decisive versus composite: a properly mature SAME-PLANT dry/wet grain shows pericarp loosening WITHOUT becoming gelatinous and slipping off, plus abundant prickle cells on actual abaxial lemma at 400×. Bob Harms published genuine documented wet-grain and compound-scope evidence in separately copyrighted research (study source links), not incorrectly CC-labelled panel media. S. vaginiflorus has short-lived annual root system and sheath flowers but field habit overlaps; retain original native county approval/holds.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: FIRST see aboveground perennial-looking Hays-region bunch habit at gallery panels 3 and 15 (indices 2,14), but NO exposed connected perennial roots are photographed there.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: The first CC0 image panel 1 (index 0) shows a REAL outside blade/sheath junction and several fine hairs, but not a true inner 0.2–0.3 mm fringe with a 1-mm bar. Bob Harms' two-view collar photo is panel 14 (index 13), with source scale at right; individual hair tips cannot safely be measured from those pixels. Panel 3 (index 2) shows aboveground tuft foliage only. Require an exposed basal fibrous root/crown connected to a flowering culm, plus a sharply focused, opened INNER fringe ligule next to calibrated 0.5–1 mm graduations.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Panels 8 and 10–11 (indices 7,9,10) show PURPLE ANTHERS exerted beyond actual green/lilac flowering units; they are pollen organs, NOT awns. Bob Harms' panel 13 (index 12) shows genuine intact/opened one-floret spikelet and separately isolated pale grains and floral bracts. Approx. 5–7 mm spikelet size and one fertile floret are PUBLISHED botanical measurements; the photographed parts have not been jointly measured and assigned to one authenticated collected individual.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

panels.label: Rough dropseed — true blade/sheath junction and visible fine hairs
panels.caption: The greenish sheath wraps a fingertip, and a dried blade angles to the right from its mouth. Very fine pale hairs are visible along the margin of the blade/sheath junction. They can guide the crew to where the true short hair-fringe ligule belongs, but the inner free edge and the published 0.2–0.3 mm length cannot be proven with this unscaled exterior view.

panels.label: Rough dropseed — tiny detached dark reproductive units
panels.caption: Two small dark pointed units from a source-labelled rough dropseed observation are placed against a palm. This gives a genuine size-context lesson and shows how unlike the whole contracted flowerhead the separated units look. The photograph does not prove glume, lemma, caryopsis, gelatinization, or a calibrated measurement.

Most decisive versus composite: a properly mature SAME-PLANT dry/wet grain shows pericarp loosening WITHOUT becoming gelatinous and slipping off, plus abundant prickle cells on actual abaxial lemma at 400×. memory_rule: ROUGH DROPSEED: PERENNIAL fine leafy tuft → long very NARROW contracted PANICLE → ONE-FLORETED, AWNLESS spikelets (ca. 5–7mm in GrassBase) → 2 BASAL glumes enclosing pubescent lemma/palea and exposed ~2–3mm grain. Truly short 0.2–0.3mm HAIR LIGULE. Fresh grain pericarp loosens but does NOT jelly/slip off like composite; lemma PRICKLES require 400×.
safety_note: 17 real gallery panels, 15 physically archived own-species JPEGs, 2 physically linked OTHER-species look-alikes and 1 externally linked historical public-domain botanical drawing in images[] (not a gallery photograph). Eleven preexisting Bob Harms copyrighted images from the Selected Central Texas Monocots collection must retain photo-specific attribution and limited educational/scientific reuse. True exposed crown, tiny inner ligule and calibrated seed/pericarp remain unproven. No county-native inference from a Hays collection general locality.
field_rule: Field recognition may proceed with narrow paniculate habit, anthers and spikelets; to separate troublesome S. clandestinus and S. compositus use mature authenticated material, actual lemma/prickle characters and fresh-grain observations when necessary. Never identify a different taxon using a single common name 'rough dropseed'.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
